notation.space: S is affine Euclidean 3-space; x denotes a position vector
notation.projection: alpha={x:n.x=c}, direction span(d), n!=0, d!=0, n.d!=0; P(x)=x-((n.x-c)/(n.d))*d
notation.source_notation_preserved: B17 literally writes $Z_0$; author Z_O names the prose centre O without correcting the source
notation.composition_order: f2 circle f1 means first f1, then f2
notation.parallelism: original line, line-plane and plane definitions include coincidence/containment; no strict-only convention is imposed

global_conditions_and_limits.claim: n.d!=0 is required for a unique projector-plane intersection; perpendicular projection is not assumed
global_conditions_and_limits.derivation: Solve n.(x+t*d)=c. If n.d=0, intersections are absent for points off alpha or nonunique for projectors in alpha.
Restrict T to W and use its one-dimensional kernel. A nondegenerate planar figure has rank 1 or 2, not 0; a full 3-dimensional solid always has rank 2.

global_conditions_and_limits.claim: Images of solid, full surface, and edge frame must be distinguished
global_conditions_and_limits.derivation: P commutes with convex hull. Endpoints of compact nonempty fibres prove P(boundary K)=P(K) for a convex 3-dimensional solid. An edge frame instead maps to a finite union of projected segments.
global_conditions_and_limits.literal_limit: Earlier original prose defers detailed polyhedron definitions. This precursor supplies explicit representation-dependent results, not a silent definition replacement.

global_conditions_and_limits.claim: The consulted original prose does not resolve exactly-one versus at-least-one parallel-side-pair terminology
global_conditions_and_limits.derivation: A rank-2 affine bijection preserves parallelism and its converse; retain the input convention. A proper trapezoid cannot newly become a parallelogram.

global_conditions_and_limits.claim: The original definition requires injectivity but not explicit surjectivity; global inverse existence is not entailed
global_conditions_and_limits.derivation: For f(x,y,z)=(g(x),y,z), g(t)=t for t<0 and t+1 for t>=0, f is injective but omits the slab 0<=x<1. Its reversed graph has no value at (1/2,0,0). The inverse h:f(S)->S always exists and h circle f=E_S.

global_conditions_and_limits.claim: Original PNG l/ell, O/0 and source M-token trailing strokes remain optically UNKNOWN where stated in the author inventory
global_conditions_and_limits.derivation: Three actual original PNGs were each inspected once at original detail. Prose notation is kept separate from pixel interpretation.

tasks.source_text: 153°. 在平行投影下，下列图形的象是什么图形？1) 三角形；2) 梯形；3) 四面体；4) 平行六面体.

subparts.author_result: Nondegenerate triangle when rank 2 on its plane; nonzero segment when rank 1.

cases.condition: d not in the direction plane of the triangle
cases.image: nondegenerate triangle; boundary or filled region follows the input convention
cases.proof: The restricted T has zero kernel, hence is an affine bijection of planes and preserves three noncollinear vertices.

cases.condition: d in the direction plane of the triangle, still n.d!=0
cases.image: nonzero segment between extreme projected vertices
cases.proof: Restricted rank is 2-1=1. Affine convex combinations give the entire interval; the connected boundary also covers the interval.
vertex_cases: One side parallel to d: that side's endpoint images coincide, the third image is different.
No side parallel to d: three distinct collinear images are possible.

subparts.excluded: Point collapse is impossible for three noncollinear original vertices under a valid projection.
subparts.existence: Both ranks occur by choosing the triangle plane transverse to, or containing the direction d; the target plane remains transverse to d.

subparts.author_result: Trapezoid when rank 2 on its plane; nonzero segment when rank 1.

cases.condition: d not in the trapezoid's direction plane
cases.image: trapezoid retaining the original convention about admitting parallelograms
cases.proof: An invertible planar affine map preserves parallel and nonparallel directions. It preserves the base length ratio by the common directional scale factor.
cases.limit: A proper trapezoid cannot become a parallelogram. No exactly-one-pair convention is added to the source.

cases.condition: d in the trapezoid's direction plane, still transverse to alpha
cases.image: nonzero segment; two, three or four distinct collinear projected vertices
cases.proof: Restricted rank is 1. The min/max of the projected vertex coordinate delimit the whole image interval.
cases.existence: For vertices (0,0),(3,0),(2,1),(0,1), scalar projections y, x, x+2y have respectively 2, 3, 4 distinct values. Their kernels can be used as a valid spatial projection direction.
cases.limit: If both projected bases collapse, do not claim a length ratio from 0/0.

subparts.excluded: A genuine trapezoid cannot collapse to a single point under a valid rank-2 spatial P.

subparts.author_result: A convex quadrilateral or a triangle for the whole nondegenerate solid or its whole surface.
subparts.proof: P(conv{A,B,C,D})=conv{A_1,B_1,C_1,D_1}. The full-dimensional tetrahedron has projected affine span 2. A convex hull of four plane points spanning a plane has three or four extreme vertices.

cases.source_example: F58 lower displayed perimeter is A_1-B_1-C_1-D_1-A_1.

cases.condition: three extreme projected points; fourth strictly inside
cases.image: triangle with an interior projected vertex

cases.condition: three extreme projected points; fourth on an edge
cases.image: triangle with an additional collinear edge point

cases.condition: exactly one projected vertex pair coincides, other projected vertices span the plane
cases.limit: Two coincident pairs or three coincident vertices would force a degenerate original affine span and are excluded.

subparts.existence_proof: For any four planar points p0...p3 spanning a plane, the 2x3 difference matrix has a one-dimensional kernel span(r). Choose lift heights h1,h2,h3 with r.h!=0 along d. The spatial difference vectors are independent and yield exactly those projections.

coordinate_examples.basis: Two target-plane directions and d form an affine basis, not an assumed orthonormal basis. P(x,y,z)=(x,y,0).

subparts.surface_proof: Every nonempty compact projector fibre through the solid has a boundary endpoint, so P(boundary K)=P(K).
subparts.edge_frame_image: Union of [A_1B_1],[A_1C_1],[A_1D_1],[B_1C_1],[B_1D_1],[C_1D_1], allowing overlaps and collapsed edges; not generally the filled hull.
excluded: No segment or point image for a nondegenerate tetrahedron.
A concave or self-crossing ordered quadrilateral is not the convex set-image.
The original worked quadrilateral example is not a universal theorem.

subparts.author_result: Nondegenerate parallelogram or centrally symmetric convex hexagon for the whole solid or its whole surface.
subparts.proof: With independent u,v,w, K=q+[0,1]u+[0,1]v+[0,1]w. Its image is P(q)+[0,1]a+[0,1]b+[0,1]c, where a=T(u),b=T(v),c=T(w) span the target plane. Nonzero generators have either two or three unoriented directions.

subcases: One generator is zero; the other two are independent.
All three are nonzero and two are parallel, including oppositely directed generators.
cases.proof: Combine parallel interval sums into one interval in that direction; the other direction supplies the second interval.

cases.condition: three nonzero pairwise nonparallel generator directions
cases.proof: Each generator direction gives two opposite support edges. Distinct directions give six edges. Coefficients t_i -> 1-t_i give centre P(q)+(a+b+c)/2.

existence_examples.basis: Affine basis of target-plane directions and d; no metric perpendicularity is imposed.
existence_examples.parallelogram_one_zero_generator: u=d, v and w independent in the target plane

subparts.surface_proof: Compact fibre endpoints prove the surface has the same filled projected region.
subparts.edge_frame_image: For each i=1,2,3 and each binary choice of the other two coefficients, use the segment from P(q)+sum(other coefficients*generators) to that point plus generator i. The union of these 12 segments may overlap or collapse but is not the filled region.
excluded: At most one projected generator vanishes.
No point or segment image for a genuine 3-dimensional parallelepiped.
No triangular, pentagonal, or octagonal silhouette.
A cube, rectangularity and generic position are not assumptions.

tasks.source_text: 154. 空间所有点的投影成平面. 这个映射是变换吗？
tasks.author_result: No: projection is not injective, and therefore is not a transformation under the original definition.
tasks.proof: For nonzero t, x and x+t*d are distinct and have equal projections. As S->alpha the map is onto alpha; treating alpha as a subset of S does not restore injectivity.
tasks.limit: This uses the original injectivity requirement, not an unprinted bijectivity requirement.

tasks.source_text: 155. 在以$A$为中心的对称下，求作四面体$ABCD$的顶点的象.
tasks.author_result: A maps to A; B,C,D map to B_1=2A-B,C_1=2A-C,D_1=2A-D.

vertex_requests.proof: The source explicitly defines the centre as symmetric to itself; no line through a zero-length AA is selected.

vertex_requests.construction: Extend AB through A onto the ray opposite AB; mark B_1 at distance |AB| from A.
vertex_requests.proof: A is the midpoint of BB_1, and the point at a positive prescribed distance on an opposite ray exists uniquely.

vertex_requests.construction: Extend AC through A onto the opposite ray; mark C_1 at distance |AC| from A.
vertex_requests.proof: A is the midpoint of CC_1; uniqueness follows from the midpoint equation.

vertex_requests.construction: Extend AD through A onto the opposite ray; mark D_1 at distance |AD| from A.
vertex_requests.proof: A is the midpoint of DD_1; uniqueness follows from the midpoint equation.

tasks.nondegeneracy_proof: The edge vectors from A are the negatives of the original independent vectors; the image vertices are distinct and noncoplanar.
tasks.image_shape: The tetrahedron A B_1 C_1 D_1 is congruent to ABCD because pairwise vector differences change sign.

tasks.source_text: 156. 在中心对称下，是否存在映射成自身的点、直线和平面？
tasks.author_result: Yes: exactly O, all lines through O, and all planes through O.

semantic_requests_not_printed_subparts.existence: The explicit centre-fixed stipulation supplies O.

semantic_requests_not_printed_subparts.proof: For ell=a+span(v), Z_O(ell)=2o-a+span(v), equal to ell iff o-a is in span(v).
semantic_requests_not_printed_subparts.existence: Any nonzero direction through O gives such a line.
semantic_requests_not_printed_subparts.centre_off_object_case: A distinct parallel line, not an invariant line.

semantic_requests_not_printed_subparts.proof: For beta={x:n.x=c}, its image is {x:n.x=2n.o-c}; equality holds iff n.o=c.
semantic_requests_not_printed_subparts.centre_off_object_case: A distinct parallel plane, not an invariant plane.

tasks.setwise_pointwise_distinction: An invariant line or plane is mapped onto itself as a set; its noncentre points are exchanged, not fixed individually.
tasks.all_invariant_sets: Q is invariant iff x in Q implies 2o-x in Q. Such sets are unions of paired points with O optionally included; empty Q is invariant.
tasks.inclusive_parallelism: Coincident invariant lines/planes are also parallel under the source convention; do not insist on distinctness.

tasks.source_text: 157°. 1) 中心对称的逆变换是怎样的变换？2) 有同一个中心的两个中心对称的合成是什么变换？

subparts.author_result: The same centre symmetry: Z_O^{-1}=Z_O on all S.
subparts.proof: Z_O(Z_O(x))=2o-(2o-x)=x. Every y has preimage 2o-y, so global inverse existence is proved.
subparts.centre_case: O maps to O in both directions.

subparts.proof: Two applications with the same centre give x -> 2o-x -> x, so Z_O circle Z_O=E.
subparts.limit: The centres are the same; no unequal-centre translation is inferred for this request.

subparts.proof: For every x in S, E(f(x))=f(x).

subparts.author_result: E_S if f^{-1} denotes the inverse defined on f(S); also E_S when a global inverse is separately known to exist.
subparts.proof: Injectivity supplies the unique h:f(S)->S with h(f(x))=x for all x in S.
subparts.literal_definition_disclosure: The original injective-self-map definition does not guarantee f(S)=S. Reading B20 as asserting a global inverse for every transformation is unjustified; without onto, that global inverse may be undefined.
subparts.counterexample: f(x,y,z)=(g(x),y,z), g(t)=t for t<0 and t+1 for t>=0, is injective and misses 0<=x<1.
subparts.opposite_composition_limit: f circle h is identity on f(S), not generally identity on all S.

derived_claims: A mapping is total and single-valued; neither injectivity nor onto is built into the mapping definition.
Image is a subset of the stated codomain, with equality explicitly allowed.
Projection fibres are x+span(d); noncollapsed planar projection is injective, spatial projection is not.
The tetrahedron quadrilateral is a particular configuration, not the only possible image.
Actual PNG inventories are in the author note and manifest.
Optical UNKNOWN labels are not resolved from theory, and solid/dashed strokes are not discarded.
Z_O(x)=2o-x exists uniquely including the centre case, is injective and onto, preserves distances and affine incidence, and is involutive.
The source transformation definition is an injective self-map; it is not silently strengthened.
The source literal $Z_0$ is preserved separately from author semantic notation Z_O.
Narrative transitions do not supply extra conditions or authorize consulting the future section.
Graph of f is {(x,f(x))}; swapped graph defines a unique inverse on f(S), globally only if onto.
Composition f2 circle f1 is total and injective, and applies f1 first.
Composition is associative; E is the two-sided identity and diagonal graph.
For bijections, inverse of f2 circle f1 is f1^{-1} circle f2^{-1}. For injections the same formula is restricted to f2(f1(S)).
Injective self-maps form a monoid under composition, not necessarily a group.
